# Desire as lack

One old picture says that desire is the mark of something missing. We want because we are incomplete, and each object stands in for an absence it can never fill.

## Consequences

If desire is lack, then satisfaction is always a disappointment: the object arrives and the absence remains. The wanting moves on to the next object. This explains the restless quality of wanting better than any theory of preferences does.

The opposing picture is in [[Desire as production]]. The two might not be rivals: lack describes how desire feels from the inside, production describes what it does.

See [[Mimetic desire]] for where the objects come from in the first place.
